title: ICE Agent Christian Castro Pleads Not Guilty to Federal Charges of Lying to FBI About Minneapolis Shooting
detail: ICE officer Christian Castro pleaded not guilty on Friday, September 18, 2026 in federal court to six counts of making false statements to the FBI regarding his January 14, 2026 shooting of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, a 24-year-old Venezuelan man, during Operation Metro Surge in Minneapolis. Federal prosecutors say Castro shot Sosa-Celis in the leg through the front door of a Minneapolis home and then falsely told investigators he had been attacked with a broom handle and a snow shovel before firing. U.S. Magistrate Judge Elizabeth Cowan Wright set bond at $75,000, requiring a GPS ankle monitor, surrender of Castro's passport and personal firearms, a 9 p.m.–6 a.m. curfew, a mental health evaluation, and travel restricted to Minnesota and Texas. Castro is the first federal law enforcement officer charged by the Justice Department with wrongdoing arising from Operation Metro Surge, and separately faces Hennepin County state charges of second-degree assault in the same shooting.

title: Costa Rican Detainee Dies at Winn Correctional Center After Family Says Insulin, Meals Were Missed
detail: Carlos Josué Marchena Marchena, a 36-year-old Costa Rican father of four with Type 1 diabetes, was found unresponsive at Winn Correctional Center in Winnfield, Louisiana on September 18, 2026; staff called a medical emergency and began life-saving measures, but he was pronounced dead around 8 a.m. at Winn Parish Medical Center. Marchena had been shuttled between ICE facilities in multiple states in the week before his death, and his family said he complained of missed insulin doses, skipped meals, and no blood-sugar monitoring; his girlfriend said he called around midnight reporting chest pain, vomiting, headaches, and chills, and that the medication he was given was insufficient. He was the third detainee to die at Winn in less than six months; a June 2026 DHS Inspector General report had already found inadequate medical record-keeping, improper food storage, and substandard medical care protocols at the facility. ICE said Marchena 'received proper medical care and was seen by medical professionals.' The cause of death is pending a medical examination, though family members and reporting outlets have pointed to suspected cardiac arrest linked to insulin mismanagement. The National Immigration Project of the National Lawyers Guild's running tally puts 2026 calendar-year deaths in ICE custody at 27 as of Marchena's death, with the case reported publicly on September 25.
